intro: Lesson 47: Reading from the mushaf: finding our surahs. To understand how a page of the mushaf is set out so I can find and follow a surah I know

arabic.text: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ (١) مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ (٢) وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ (٣) يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ (٤) وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ (٥)

questions.q: Find Al-'Asr in your mushaf and point to its three ayah circles.
questions.a: Al-'Asr found; three circles pointed to.
questions.model: I do: Juz' 'Amma, near the end; the box says Al-'Asr; I touch circle 1, 2, 3.

questions.q: Find and follow: read Al-Qari'ah from the mushaf with your finger while the teacher reads. Today's group reads one ayah each to the teacher.
questions.a: Finger follows each word; the group reads aloud in turn.
questions.model: The teacher reads 101:1 with a finger on the shared page.

questions.q: count the lines Al-'Asr takes up in your mushaf.
questions.a: Usually one or two lines (depends on the printing).

questions.q: A surah starts with its name and ...
Back to our ponder: The mushaf has hundreds of pages. How could you find Al-Qari'ah quickly?
questions.a: Look near the end: Juz' 'Amma. Each surah starts with its name in a box and Bismillah.
